code_verdict: CONDITIONALLY APPROVED, code only (not data integration). I read the full bundle: realizations.py, baseline.py, build.py, test_marmorstein_realizations.py and test_marmorstein_baseline.py. Every v3 finding is resolved. (1) MEDIUM v3: prepare_documents only accepts PLAIN_SEGMENT_KEYS on the host. It then removes every mapping key, checks that the pointer's keys are within CANONICAL_OCCURRENCE_KEYS, and runs validate_occurrence_controls. validate_occurrences also checks the effective context returned first by prepare_documents, so generated pointers now get the full canonical-occurrence validation. test_home_retains_verse_metadata_while_context_pointer_is_plain covers removal from the pointer, retention on the home, a verse-part milestone in the home XML, deep-copy isolation, and an unknown key raising an error. (2) LOW v3, condition_end_corresp: build.py and attesting_controls both resolve the endpoint only through corresp and skip transcludes. validate_redirection rejects any condition_end_corresp, repeat, transclude, repeat_cue, citation or order target that names a redirected identity, and test_redirection_preflight_checks_controls_and_interpretations tests this. I accept this as consistent. (3) LOW v3, citations: there is now a passing baseline, a passing external `reference`, and target/targetEnd/reference failures checked against specific messages. (4) LOW v3, flag test: I confirmed in build.py that a bare biblical corresp opens a chapter milestone automatically (the `if biblical:` branch calls close_references() and then emits milestone unit=chapter n=…). The test's filter (no @corresp, no @n) therefore correctly isolates the verse+chapter or prayer-part closures before the note, and the note sits right before the pointer. One new MEDIUM gap blocks unconditional approval: attesting_controls does not bind attesters of whole-text targets (see below). Fix it, or add a hard guard, before final approval. The other items are LOW.

findings.reason: attesting_controls (about lines 46-78) walks the raw `unit['languages']` segments, not the effective documents, even though its docstring says it binds 'effective occurrence scopes'. This misses attesters in two ways. (a) A unit-level `canonical_whole` occurrence only turns into a `canonical` segment inside prepare_unit. Its raw segments have no `canonical`, so it never shows up as an attester, and neither do its unit conditions, instructions or head. (b) Explicit pointers whose target is a whole-text identity (text_corresp or canonical_home.text_corresp) get `covered = {target}` (about line 69). review_payloads (about line 410) passes `selected_ids = {segment_identity(v) for v in selected}`, which holds only the host's segment identities (Bible ids or None) and never the text_corresp. The intersection is always empty. So when another attester's condition changes for a whole formula, the caller's receipt stays valid without any warning. Segment-identity targets, ranges and pure parts work correctly.
findings.required_fix: In review_payloads, add `target` to the identities passed to attesting_controls when _range_segments matched by whole-text identity. Alternatively, compute `covered` the same way for both sides. In attesting_controls, walk effective segments, for example `prepare_documents(unit, readings)[0]['languages']`, instead of raw segments, and keep the raw segment indexes for scope endpoints. Add a test: host with text_corresp, one caller using canonical_whole and one using an explicit canonical=text_corresp pointer, each with a condition; changing either condition must change the other caller's realization payload. If you defer the fix, make attesting_controls raise when any canonical_whole or whole-text target exists, so it cannot be silently wrong.

findings.reason: validate_redirection's docstring says it rejects 'controls that a new pointer would lose'. It only rejects source_reference_part plus keys outside PLAIN_SEGMENT_KEYS ∪ OCCURRENCE_CONTROL_KEYS. So a segment carrying source, source_reference, source_reference_corresp, chapter_corresp or source_reference_end passes the preflight. A redirected pointer cannot keep any of these, because CANONICAL_OCCURRENCE_KEYS excludes them. In build.py they render quotation seg, chapter and verse milestones, so dropping them loses markup unless someone moves them to the host by hand. end_reference and reference_unit are harmless to drop, since a canonical segment always calls close_references. As a result, `allowed_mapping_only: true` does not prove that the mapping is preserved.
findings.required_fix: In validate_redirection, reject the redirected segment if it has any of source, source_reference, source_reference_corresp, chapter_corresp or source_reference_end (allow corresp, end_reference, reference_unit and paragraph). Or return the list of mapping keys that must be moved to the host, so the integration step can assert that the host has them. Add a preflight test case with source_reference on PARTS[0].

A second unit attests through canonical=segment1, canonical_end=segment2 and has a condition. findings.reason: test_invalid_conditions_and_orphan_condition_rubric_fail uses one alternation regex for all cases, 'typed feature structures|requires conditions|one plain source fragment'. None of the three cases can reach 'one plain source fragment', because conditions and condition_instruction are in CANONICAL_OCCURRENCE_KEYS. The extra alternative lets a regression that rejects these at the key gate still pass.
findings.required_fix: Expect a specific message per case: conditions=[{}] and conditions='unmodeled' should give 'typed feature structures', and the orphan condition_instruction should give 'requires conditions'.

findings.reason: In build()'s per-unit document loop: `pending = pending or any(not review_is_current(reviews.get(key, {}), payload) for key, payload in realization_payloads.items())`. Any stale realization anywhere in the book puts the DRAFT label on every unit that has a realization payload, instead of checking that unit's own `realization_key`. This only affects the labelling in --draft mode, and it errs on the side of caution, but it contradicts the per-unit realization_key computed on the line before.
findings.required_fix: Use `not review_is_current(reviews.get(realization_key, {}), realization_payloads[realization_key])`. If the broad check is deliberate, add a comment saying so.
